mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the long-run mean at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that erodes real purchasing power and increases interest costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed thresholds, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the joint effect is not statistically significant in a bivariate regression.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered periods, or the median return is not above the long-run mean at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the median return is not above zero at 95% confidence.
